pageCache.pageTitle: WELCOME TO THE ORATORY PREP SCHOOL | Oratory Prep
pageCache.text:
WELCOME TO THE ORATORY PREP SCHOOL
Welcome to The Oratory Prep School. We are a busy, happy school where children are at the centre of everything. With 65 acres of space and outstanding facilities, there’s Space to Learn and Room to Grow. We believe in setting high standards, but always with the right support. Pupils are known and encouraged as individuals. Learning here is purposeful, challenging and fun. From the classroom to the stage, the forest school to the swimming pool, we want children to enjoy every day and feel proud of what they achieve. Because we’re a school for ages 2 to 13, our pupils grow up in a setting that feels like home and where children can be children for longer. Our older pupils lead with kindness and set the tone for a community built on encouragement and care. They leave us confident, curious and ready for what’s next.
EXPERIENCE
We make the most of real-world learning. Trips and residentials are woven through the year groups. These shared experiences help children build friendships, develop resilience and apply their learning in different contexts.
As a boarding school we welcome pupils from all over the world which means our pupils connect with cultures beyond their own. They are encouraged to think outwardly and engage with the world around them, learning to question, reflect and contribute with empathy.
Co-curricular life is full and varied, with clubs and activities running before, during and after school. Every pupil is encouraged to try something new and follow their interests.
LEARNING JOURNEY
We know that confidence in learning often comes from feeling secure, understood and supported. Small class sizes, specialist teaching and strong relationships mean we can stretch, support and challenge your children as individuals. Our curriculum is ambitious, broad and carefully sequenced giving pupils the skills and knowledge they need to succeed.
Excellent teaching sits at the heart of everything we do. Lessons are purposeful and engaging with plenty of scope for discussion, collaboration and creativity. Pupils are encouraged to reflect on their progress and take ownership of their learning.
COMMUNITY
Community is more than just a word at The Oratory Prep School – it is something you feel from the moment you arrive. There is a strong sense of belonging, built over time through shared routines and the way everyone is known and valued.
Parents are a vital part of school life too and there are many ways to get involved. We work closely with families to help support and celebrate your child’s progress.
Boarding adds another layer to our community. Pupils from Year 3 upwards can board weekly or flexibly, depending on what suits your family. Even a single night of boarding can help build independence and the boarding house has a warmth and rhythm all of its own.
Little Oaks Nursery
At Little Oaks Nursery, we’re all about nurturing young explorers in a warm, friendly environment where curiosity and discovery come to life.
Nestled in the heart of The Oratory Prep School’s beautiful 65-acre campus, Little Oaks gives children (ages 2-4) the perfect place to begin their learning journey.
Pre-Prep
Life in Pre-Prep is enriched with engaging activities that extend beyond the classroom.
Pupils participate in Sparkling Starts that ignite curiosity at the beginning of topics and Phenomenal Finishes, where they proudly present their learning to their parents and peers.
Prep
In Prep, pupils become ambitious and independent learners, immersed in a skills-based, interconnected curriculum, meaningful and highly relevant to their everyday experiences and life beyond school.
We enable our children to make connections across subjects and think more deeply about their significance, applying their learning across different contexts and developing core, transferable skills, such as critical thinking and strong reasoning skills.

A School for the Whole Family School life isn’t just about...

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep Music & Drama | Prep School Oxfordshire | Oratory Prep
pageCache.text:
The Arts are a key part of school life, helping our pupils build confidence, express themselves and work together. Our inclusive approach means everyone, no matter their experience or ability, has the chance to shine. We are proud of our excellent teachers who nurture talent and inspire a lifelong love of the arts. In 2024, we were highly commended in the Muddy Stilettos Schools Awards for Dynamic Performing Arts, a testament to our vibrant programme.
Music
Music at The Oratory Prep School is taught with the aim of developing the enjoyment of the subject within every child, whether as a performer, listener or composer. We have a purpose-built music department complete with a suite of practice rooms, a large rehearsal room with a vast array of instruments and a music tech room. Pupils have the opportunity to learn instruments, join choirs and instrumental groups. Every term we enjoy concerts showcasing the abilities of our pupils and parents have many occasions to watch their children perform.
Drama
We make the most of our modern theatre with its large stage, 300-seater auditorium and state of the art sound and lighting systems. This is home to weekly drama lessons giving pupils a platform to build confidence and step out of their comfort zone to take on roles that will extend and challenge them on stage. We encourage creativity and collaboration as our drama productions are pupil-led both on stage and off. Dance and Lamda lessons further enhance self-expression and confidence, with outstanding results, including numerous distinctions and scholarships.
Art
The Art Department is guided by the mantra Explore, Experiment and Express. Every child has a unique creative voice and we provide a rich variety of opportunities to help them discover it. Pupils are fortunate to have access to an exceptional range of artistic disciplines from ceramics, sculpture and painting to screen printing, street art and textiles which allows them to develop diverse creative skills and techniques. The wider school community is deeply supportive of the arts and throughout the year we host numerous events that celebrate creativity and collaboration across departments. Our Art Scholarship programme further enriches talented pupils with additional opportunities, including off-site trips designed to inspire and challenge their artistic development. Above all, we aim to nurture not only excellence but also the imagination and freedom of expression that lie at the heart of every young artist.
Our Virtual Tour
Set within 65 acres of countryside, on the borders of Berkshire and Oxfordshire, The Oratory Prep School is a thriving place for children to learn and grow into happy, grounded and self-assured individuals, each with a unique sense of purpose.
We invite you to take a virtual tour of our school below and discover our outstanding facilities and extensive outdoor areas.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep Curriculum | Prep School Berkshire | Oratory Prep
pageCache.text:
At The Oratory Prep School, our curriculum is designed to inspire curiosity, provide challenge and foster a lifelong love of learning. Taught by subject specialists, pupils benefit from expert teaching across all areas of the curriculum. From exploring historical events to conducting scientific experiments, lessons are engaging, stimulating and designed to stretch and support pupils at every level.
Learning is interconnected and purposeful, with meaningful links between subjects that deepen understanding. Mathematical skills are applied in science investigations, while literature choices reflect historical periods, bringing topics to life. With a focus on both engagement and academic rigour, our pupils are consistently challenged through thought-provoking lessons and regular, thorough assessments that track progress and inform next steps.
Scholarships at The Oratory Prep School
At The Oratory Prep School, scholarships celebrate excellence, commitment, and potential. They are awarded to pupils entering Year 7, based on their performance in assessments during Year 6, with opportunities available in Academics, Art, Music and Sport.
Scholarships are about recognising and nurturing exceptional talent, with a focus on supporting each scholar’s growth, rather than providing a large financial reward. However, they do carry a small fee remission or financial award (at the Headmaster’s discretion) to help further develop the pupil’s expertise in their chosen field.
Scholarships are reviewed annually, taking into account a child’s achievement and dedication in their specialism, as well as their overall effort, attitude and behaviour.
All candidates are considered for every specialism and will be interviewed by our Director of Studies, Miss Claire Knights, as part of the selection process.
Key Dates for 2026-2027 Scholarships
External Candidates
Parents are advised to speak to their child’s current school, so that they are aware of the application and can identify the pupil as a potential Scholar, as well as offer appropriate support.
In order to be considered for an award, applicants must be registered for a place at The Oratory Prep School. Please get in touch with our Admissions Department for more information or read the booklet below.

Set within 65 acres of countryside, on the borders of Berkshire and Oxfordshire, The Oratory Prep School is a thriving place for children to learn and grow into happy, grounded and self-assured individuals, each with a unique sense of purpose.
We invite you to take a virtual tour of our school below and discover our outstanding facilities and extensive outdoor areas.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headmaster’s Welcome | Prep School Reading | Oratory Prep
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headmaster
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions you will make as a family. It is about finding a place where your child will be happy, known as an individual and strive to be the best version of themselves.
That is exactly what drew my family and me to The Oratory Prep School.
From my very first visit, I was struck by the warmth of the community. There is a genuine sense that every child matters here. Children are supported to be curious, to challenge themselves and to grow in confidence, all within an environment where kindness and strong relationships are at the heart of school life.
Throughout my career, I have had the privilege of teaching children from Nursery through to A Level in both co-educational and single-sex schools. Those experiences, alongside leadership roles including running a boarding house and most recently serving as Head of Prep School, have reinforced my belief that the best schools see every child as an individual. When children feel valued and understood, they develop the confidence to embrace new opportunities and achieve more than they ever thought possible.
Joining The Oratory Prep School is a family adventure for us. My wife, Becky, has joined the Admissions Team and will also be teaching sport, while our two daughters are excited to begin their own journey here as pupils. We have already received such a warm welcome and are looking forward to becoming part of this wonderful community.
Set within 65 acres of South Oxfordshire countryside, The Oratory Prep School offers children the space to learn, play and grow. Outstanding teaching sits alongside exceptional pastoral care, while opportunities in sport, music, drama, art and outdoor learning allow every child to discover new interests and develop lasting confidence.
We are proud of the academic outcomes our pupils achieve and the wide range of senior schools they move on to. Just as importantly, we want every child to leave us with curiosity, resilience, compassion and the confidence to make the most of whatever comes next.
Whether you are considering Little Oaks Nursery, joining us in Reception or looking at entry later in your child’s education, I would be delighted to welcome you to the school. The best way to understand what makes The Oratory Prep School so special is to come and experience it for yourself.
I look forward to meeting you and your family.
Mr William May Headmaster
“Everyone has been so supportive throughout our entire journey and we feel very blessed to be part of the school family.”

pageCache.pageTitle: History | Prep School Berkshire | Oratory Prep
pageCache.text:
The Oratory Prep School traces its origins to Saint John Henry Newman, a former Anglican Oxford intellectual who became a Catholic and was later made a Cardinal. He was canonised by Pope Francis during an open-air Mass in Rome on 13th October 2019.
The school opened on 2nd May 1859 with nine boys on roll, all of prep school age. In 1922, The Oratory School moved to Caversham Park near Reading. Three years on, and less than a mile away, The Oratory Prep School opened with just four boys at Rose Hill House, a Georgian-style mansion in Emmer Green. The first Headmaster was Father Sebastian Ritchie and by 1930 there were 30 boys.
In 1938, ill health forced Father Ritchie’s retirement and mounting financial difficulties meant that Rose Hill had to be sold and the Oratory Prep School took the top floor of Caversham Park with 15 boys and Ronald Richings as Head. By 1940 there were over 50 boys.
In 1941, Caversham Park was sold and The Oratory Prep School merged with Worth Preparatory School at a temporary wartime home at Downside. After only two terms, The Oratory School re-established itself at Woodcote House and three cottages in Exlade Street forming a school for a small number of younger boys aged 10 to 13, pending the opening of a new Prep School.
In 1946, The Oratory Prep School reopened its doors to 35 boys at the ‘Old Ryde’, a mansion at the Branksome Park end of Poole. The Headmaster was Antony Patton. He was succeeded by Cyril Bull and then in 1958 by Christopher Maude.
Maude’s retirement in 1968 coincided with the move from Branksome to the Prep School’s current site in Crays Pond. This was only two miles from The Oratory School and the former home of the Prep School to St Mary’s, Wantage. The nuns had converted and extended the billiards room of the house into a chapel for their services and it was reconsecrated as a Catholic Chapel in 1968. Ever since, it has been used for Mass as part of the school’s Catholic life. Ninety five boys from Branksome joined with 25 from Elston Hall near Newark, bringing the numbers up to their highest ever.
Patrick Stow was now the Headmaster and in 1970 a Pre-Preparatory Department opened with 21 pupils, including girls for the first time. George Robertson was appointed Headmaster from 1977 to 1981. The headship of Michael Randell from 1981 to 1991 marked the beginning of major projects and building developments, further accelerated under Sexon’s headship between 1991 and 2006. The school became fully co-educational and total numbers grew to over 400 pupils. On David’s retirement, Richard Hillier became Headmaster for the next four years. When, in 2010, Hillier took over the headship at the Yehudi Menuhin International Music School, Joseph Smith became the eleventh Headmaster, followed by Rob Stewart, former teacher and housemaster at Eton, who took over as Headmaster in January 2017.
In September 2022, Andrew De Silva, former Head of the Junior School at St Edmund’s School in Canterbury, became the thirteenth Headmaster of The Oratory Prep School. In September 2026, Mr William May, joins as Headmaster having previously been Head of Prep at The Marist School, Ascot.

“A stimulating and vibrant learning community”
Independent Schools Inspectorate Report 2025
We are proud to share the findings of our most recent Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) inspection, which took place in February 2025.
The report recognises a school community where pupils thrive both academically and personally. Inspectors praised the strong relationships across the school, the breadth and ambition of the curriculum and the values of kindness, curiosity and wisdom that underpin daily life.
Pupils were commended for their motivation and self-awareness. Leaders were praised for creating a culture where pupils have faith in themselves, develop intellectual curiosity and are where they are well supported to succeed in all areas of school life.
We are delighted that the inspection team captured the spirit of The Oratory Prep School: a place where children are encouraged to grow into thoughtful, capable young people.
The full report and a summary version are available to read below.
Visit Us

pageCache.pageTitle: What Others Say | Independent School Berkshire | Oratory Prep
pageCache.text:
The best way to get a feel for our school is to come and see it in action but we’re always pleased when others take the time to visit and share their thoughts.
We’ve been delighted to welcome visitors from a range of publications in recent years who review independent schools. Here is just a small selection of the kind words they’ve shared about The Oratory Prep School.
“I am delighted with my child’s progress, his friendships and his opportunities.”
“OPS is very clear about both who it is and where it’s going. It prepares children for a rapidly changing future by rooting them in school tradition while giving them the confidence to try new ways of thinking, doing and being. The fabulous rural setting, friendly atmosphere and dedicated teaching body make it a solid choice for those seeking a traditional yet forward-thinking co-ed 13+ prep school, with excellent wraparound care and flexible boarding options.”
“The OPS is a bucolic beauty with a strong identity. Although rooted in tradition, it’s just progressive enough for the kids to adapt with confidence in a modern world. We love the school’s passion for outdoor learning, its friendly, nurturing vibe and all delivered with a sprinkling of pizazz.”
“Curiosity is the cornerstone of learning here, from the black, LED-lit corridor of curiosity to tackling topics through enquiring questions – such as ‘Was the role of women as important as men’s during the Second World War?’ – rather than teachers telling pupils what’s what. Everything is approached through curiosity.”
Read the Talk Education Review
Our View
This small Oxfordshire prep makes no apology for making kindness the beating heart of school life – and what a beautiful butterfly effect this has. The warmth and good manners of everyone create such a relaxed and happy environment that it’s impossible not to feel completely at ease inside the glorious 65-acre campus. It’s the perfect space for young minds to flourish, and with pupils’ curiosity piqued at every step of their educational journey – there’s even an actual ‘corridor of curiosity’ complete with code-breaking boxes, plasma balls and distorting mirrors – Oratory Prep girls and boys can’t help but gain heaps of self-confidence, a strong moral compass and bags of enthusiasm for learning.
Where?
An easy drive from Oxford, the school sits between the villages of Goring and Woodcote in stunning countryside, with the picturesque, half-timbered main school building overlooking endless pitches, Astros, courts and a wonderful forest school that every pupil attends all the way through to Year 8. A warren of corridors and classrooms makes the large school building feel like the family home it used to be, while the separate pre-prep’s low-level buildings, with plans to refurbish the Old Barn, offer the perfect start for nursery-age children.
Head
Charismatic and outgoing, Andrew De Silva is always at the gate every morning with his Labradoodle Elgar, greeting pupils and parents, and taking the time to chat with everyone he meets. He’s definitely one of the most on-it heads we’ve met, and charmingly quirky – his office shelves are filled with Lego models that pupils are allowed to play with, and there’s a grand piano in there on which he knocks out tunes, often singing along (he was a schoolboy chorister). He and Elgar have their own Instagram account, Doodle and the Headmaster.
Mr De Silva joined the school in 2022 from St Edward’s Canterbury, and he has also held three state-school headships. He tells us he sees few differences between the state and private sectors – both are striving to prepare children for real life. ‘These children are the role models of the future, and they need to boss it,’ he says. He encourages staff to think like a child; he doesn’t want children to fear adults – our pupil guides tell us that relationships with teachers are stronger than ever and they all feel happier and more supported since his arrival. For his part, Mr De Silva is proud of how the children embody the school virtues of being wise, kind and curious, and aren’t afraid of making mistakes and learning from them.
Admissions
The school is non-selective and officially Catholic, but all or no faiths are welcome. Since Mr De Silva took over the headship in 2022, the school has been growing year on year by 10 per cent, and it’s on the cusp of needing another reception class. It was heavily oversubscribed this year, and enquiries are already outpacing last year’s. From reception upwards, all prospective pupils come in to school for a taster day and interview with the head, and from Year 2 they are asked to sit a CAT4 assessment. There is some testing of cognitive ability to ensure a fit but, says Mr De Silva, ‘we are not a school for alphas. Children who do not seem kind won’t get a place – we look for children who will contribute to the school.’
Little Oaks & Pre-Prep
Set within its own pocket of the Oratory campus, the pre-prep runs from nursery (based in the Little Oaks building) through kindergarten and Reception to Year 2. The ethos here is about stretching rather than stressful, which means top-notch pastoral care (the department has its own learning support teacher) and days filled with fun activities that lay the groundwork for learning.
Mornings begin with a prayer, exercise and an assembly followed by, in Reception, Years 1 and 2, lessons in English and maths (as well as science, music, PE and dance). Everyone has the chance to take part in forest school and more specialist teaching is added as children move up the years. Lunch is home-cooked (we hear that fish and chip Friday is a favourite); and the whole pre-prep relay, where mixed-age and ability teams compete, is a highlight of sports day.
Academics and destinations
Curiosity is the cornerstone of learning here, from the black, LED-lit corridor of curiosity to tackling topics through enquiring questions – such as ‘Was the role of women as important as men’s during the Second World War?’ – rather than teachers telling pupils what’s what. Everything is approached through curiosity. When it comes to AI, for example, it is being embraced as a tool to support human intelligence, with a new innovation lab opening soon to maximise its potential but also to teach pupils about the negatives.
Mr De Silva wants learning to be enjoyable, not something to be feared. The approach is bearing fruit; last year there was very positive feedback from senior schools, reporting that pupils are arriving academically strong and confident. Pupils sit Common Entrance in maths, English and science and roughly follow the CE syllabus in other subjects. Mr De Silva teaches Year 5s non-verbal reasoning, ethics and philosophy as part of their future schools programme. He is deeply involved in ensuring every child gets into the right senior school, meeting with families and speaking to senior admissions teams on a weekly basis. Invariably, pupils get into their first choices, such as Abingdon, Wellington, Downe House, Sherborne and The Oratory. It’s a wide range of destinations; in fact, last year no more than two pupils went to any one school, with 36 per cent winning scholarships and exhibitions.
Co-curricular
There’s an inclusive attitude to sport, with every child in Years 3 to 8 getting match experience in games from rugby, netball and cricket to football, hockey and tennis. Since director of sport Ben Bentley arrived two years ago, fixtures have multiplied. Mr Bentley also has an eye for talent, and more senior schools are now visiting the school on the lookout for potential sports scholars. Cross-country is run around the school’s own forest, and there’s an indoor pool where pupils do swimming throughout the year.
Music and drama are also strong. We were treated to an impromptu performance of Elgar’s ‘Ave Verum Corpus’ by a few members of the chamber choir (accompanied on piano by Mr De Silva) in the school’s lovely theatre. They were good! There are several choirs and an invitational orchestra too. Around a third of pupils do LAMDA lessons; they achieved an impressive 62 distinctions in exams last year. The art rooms were gloriously messy, with some impressive work on display. Pupils love the subject and the art club, called Creative Chat, is very popular, as are football and rowing clubs and ‘relaxed’ swimming.
Boarding
A new head of boarding, Leanne Spencer, has been revitalising the school’s offering, which can be anything from full to weekly to flexi. Full boarders include a mix of international and military-family pupils – there are 26 at the moment, with 30 flexi boarders. Pupils can board from Year 3, and dorms are split into junior and senior. As well as Ms Spencer, there is an all-day nurse and four live-in gappies. A big shared common room has a huge TV screen, with a games room to the side that has table football, snooker and games consoles. There’s also a small kitchen area.
On Saturday mornings, Year 5 to 8 boarders take part in the enrichment Newman Programme, which is also open to day pupils. Varied activities include Warhammer, frisbee and talks from guest speakers. The pupils also publish their own newspaper. Sundays are for outings – bowling, laser tag and graffiti-art workshops are just a few. And in the evenings, they do karaoke, bake or watch a film.
School community
Pastoral care is exceptional, with a school-wide system in which every pupil has a profile to which every teacher contributes. ‘Other schools have these systems, but we actually use them,’ says Mr De Silva. ‘Niggles’ are picked up early before they grow into problems, and in the boarding house there’s a ‘worries and suggestions’ box. Parents are very much part of the school community. Mr De Silva meets families one to one to help understand their needs, and parents are involved in swimming and tennis groups. Events such as fireworks night are well attended.
And finally….
A Catholic country prep where the mantra ‘Have faith in yourself’ is lived and breathed from the top down. Life skills are folded into everything here and, as a result, pupils’ success in every area is soaring. With more and more top senior schools looking to The Oratory Prep for talent, it’s definitely one to put on your shortlist.

pageCache.text:
At The Oratory Prep School, we believe that fresh air, exploration and hands-on experiences are essential to a child’s early development. With 65 acres of South Oxfordshire countryside on our doorstep, outdoor learning is part of everyday life at Little Oaks – and trust us, our little ones certainly get their step count in!
Every day brings new opportunities to discover something different. Children build dens, hunt for minibeasts, splash through puddles, climb, balance, collect natural treasures and watch the changing seasons unfold around them. Time outdoors sparks curiosity, encourages imagination and helps children make sense of the world in a way that simply can’t be replicated indoors.
Outdoor learning also plays an important role in developing confidence and resilience. Children learn to work together, assess risks, solve problems and become increasingly independent, all while enjoying the freedom that comes with having so much space to explore.
As part of The Oratory Prep School, Little Oaks children enjoy regular Forest School sessions led by experienced staff, as well as access to the exceptional grounds and facilities that make every day an adventure.
We don’t see outdoor learning as a break from education. It’s where some of the richest learning happens.
A World of Nature to Discover
Our purpose-built nursery is designed for curious explorers. From our cosy, enclosed playground, children step right into the wonders of our secure woods, where each day brings a new adventure. Whether they’re collecting leaves, spotting wildlife or discovering the magic of the seasons, children are always encouraged to follow their sense of wonder.
Led by Nature-Loving Experts
Our staff are true outdoor enthusiasts who know how to turn every session into a learning adventure. With tree climbing, den building and habitat hunting, they help children embrace challenges, take safe risks and build a lifelong love for the outdoors. These activities encourage independence, confidence, and resilience, all while sparking curiosity and joy.
Growing Through Play and Discovery
Outdoor learning isn’t just an add-on at The Oratory Prep School, it’s at the heart of our philosophy. We know the benefits firsthand: children who spend time outdoors tend to be more focused, creative, and socially engaged. When children have time to explore the woods, get muddy or have a quiet moment under a tree, outdoor play helps them grow in every way.
At Little Oaks we don’t just talk about nature – we live it every day. Come join us, and see your child thrive with the freedom and excitement of learning in the great outdoors.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Sport & Swimming | Private School Oxfordshire | Oratory Prep
pageCache.text:
At The Oratory Prep School we know that young children are always on the move and we’re here to channel that energy in the best way possible! For our youngest children, sport isn’t just about building skills – it’s about having fun, developing confidence and discovering all the ways they can move, stretch and play.
PE with Specialist Coaches
Our little ones start their journey with PE lessons led by our specialist sports staff, who know just how to engage young children in activities that feel like play but build essential skills including balancing, hopping, running and kicking a ball. Each lesson is designed to help your child develop coordination, strength, and confidence.
Making a Splash in the Pool
As soon as they turn three, our children get to start weekly swimming sessions in our safe and warm training pool. Our swimming teachers help them learn basic water skills and become comfortable in the water. Our focus is on making swimming fun and building confidence. Every year we offer a chance for parents to watch a swimming session in action so you can see how much progress your child is making.
Dancing to the Beat
Every week our children enjoy dance sessions in the Dance Studio with our visiting Dance teacher. Dancing helps little ones build rhythm, flexibility and balance. It’s a joyful way for them to express themselves, get activy and develop coordination – and they absolutely love it!
Get in Touch

At The Oratory Prep School, we understand that family life can be busy. Our after school clubs and wraparound care are designed to support parents while giving pupils a happy, purposeful end to the day.
Our wide range of school clubs and activities offers something for every interest, with opportunities to explore creativity, build confidence and enjoy time with friends in a safe, nurturing environment.
Take a look below at our Clubs & Activities Brochure for the MichaelmasTerm 2026 to see the full range of after school activities available.

A School for the Whole Family
School life isn’t just about the children. Of course, they’re at the heart of everything we do, but over the years we’ve seen so many friendships grow between parents too. It might start with a conversation at the school gates, while watching a match or over a cup of coffee at an event. Before long, those familiar faces become the people you look forward to seeing each day.
That’s something we’re incredibly proud of.
We want families to feel part of our community from the moment they join The Oratory Prep School, which is why we offer a range of activities for parents throughout the week.
Whether you fancy a swim before work, enjoy a game of tennis, would like to dust off your hockey stick or football boots, or simply love to sing, there’s something to get involved in.
Our current parent clubs include:
The wonderful thing is that these groups bring together parents from right across the school. Whether your child has just started in Little Oaks or is preparing to leave in Year 8, everyone is welcome.
You don’t have to be an expert either. These clubs about taking an hour for yourself, having a laugh and getting to know other parents.
When people talk about the sense of community at OPS, this is what they mean. A school where children are known as individuals and where parents quickly feel that they belong too.
We hope you’ll come along and join us.

pageCache.pageTitle: Boarding Options | Prep School Berkshire | Oratory Prep
pageCache.text:
At The Oratory Prep School boarding is an integral and enriching part of school life, offering a warm, family-oriented environment for pupils from Year 3 (age 7) upwards. Our boarding options: full, weekly and flexi, cater to every family, providing a supportive and fun experience.
Your School Family
Our boarding house is located in the heart of the school and offers comfortable accommodation for up to 50 pupils. With separate areas for boys and girls, boarders live in rooms that range from three to eight children, with opportunities to personalise their space. The house becomes a true home after school hours with the school grounds transforming into a vast playground, including 65 acres of fields, woodlands and outdoor adventure spaces.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pre-Prep Curriculum | Nursery Oxfordshire | Oratory Prep
pageCache.text:
The early years of school should inspire curiosity, build confidence and nurture a genuine love of learning. In Pre-Prep at The Oratory Prep School, every child is known as an individual and encouraged to develop at their own pace in an environment where they feel happy, secure and ready to thrive.
As part of the wider school community from their very first day, our youngest pupils benefit from specialist teaching, outstanding facilities and the sense of belonging that comes from being part of one school. Swimming lessons, Forest School, Music, PE, French and whole-school events all form part of everyday life, helping children grow in confidence and feel at home from the very beginning.
A joyful start to learning
Our broad curriculum combines excellent teaching with hands-on experiences that bring learning to life. Children are encouraged to ask questions, solve problems, be creative and discover their own interests, while small class sizes ensure every child receives the right balance of support and challenge.
Our partnership with parents begins at the classroom door. Each morning, families bring their children directly into the classroom, giving them time to settle and providing valuable opportunities for informal conversations with teachers. Those daily moments help build strong relationships and ensure every child starts the day feeling confident and ready to learn. In Reception, our parent app also shares regular updates and photographs, giving families a wonderful insight into life at school.
The school day finishes at 3.30pm, with a wide range of optional clubs from 4.00pm to 5.00pm, including yoga, fencing, baking and Spanish. After School Club runs until 6.00pm, providing a relaxed, caring environment where children can play, unwind and enjoy time with friends.

pageCache.text:
At The Oratory Prep School learning doesn’t stop at the end of a lesson. Our rich and varied extra-curricular programme gives every pupil the chance to explore, create, move and, most importantly, have fun. There’s something for everyone.
We offer over 50 clubs and activities each term, run by passionate teachers and skilled external providers. From sports to science, music to mindfulness, our clubs are designed to stretch imaginations, build confidence and spark new interests. Many take place during the school day, while others run before school, at lunchtime or after school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep Curriculum | Prep School Berkshire | Oratory Prep
pageCache.text:
At The Oratory Prep School, our curriculum is designed to inspire curiosity, provide challenge and foster a lifelong love of learning. Taught by subject specialists, pupils benefit from expert teaching across all areas of the curriculum. From exploring historical events to conducting scientific experiments, lessons are engaging, stimulating and designed to stretch and support pupils at every level.
Learning is interconnected and purposeful, with meaningful links between subjects that deepen understanding. Mathematical skills are applied in science investigations, while literature choices reflect historical periods, bringing topics to life. With a focus on both engagement and academic rigour, our pupils are consistently challenged through thought-provoking lessons and regular, thorough assessments that track progress and inform next steps.
Scholarships at The Oratory Prep School
At The Oratory Prep School, scholarships celebrate excellence, commitment, and potential. They are awarded to pupils entering Year 7, based on their performance in assessments during Year 6, with opportunities available in Academics, Art, Music and Sport.
Scholarships are about recognising and nurturing exceptional talent, with a focus on supporting each scholar’s growth, rather than providing a large financial reward. However, they do carry a small fee remission or financial award (at the Headmaster’s discretion) to help further develop the pupil’s expertise in their chosen field.
Scholarships are reviewed annually, taking into account a child’s achievement and dedication in their specialism, as well as their overall effort, attitude and behaviour.
All candidates are considered for every specialism and will be interviewed by our Director of Studies, Miss Claire Knights, as part of the selection process.
Key Dates for 2026-2027 Scholarships
External Candidates
Parents are advised to speak to their child’s current school, so that they are aware of the application and can identify the pupil as a potential Scholar, as well as offer appropriate support.
In order to be considered for an award, applicants must be registered for a place at The Oratory Prep School. Please get in touch with our Admissions Department for more information or read the booklet below.
